h1: The Davis Bangkok — Thai Heritage Boutique on a Lush 2.3-Acre Estate in Sukhumvit Soi 24
intro: If you picture Sukhumvit as nothing but glass towers, megamalls and gridlocked traffic, The Davis Bangkok will quietly change that. Tucked behind a green canopy on a 2.3-acre plot at Soi 24, it blends a modern Corner Wing with Baan Davis — a cluster of traditional Thai-style villas where the word "hotel" almost feels too small. Two outdoor pools, a spa, fitness facilities and the Fairway Golf & City Club all share the same grounds, while Emporium Shopping Mall is a 13-minute walk and the entire EM District sits within easy reach. Rates from approx. ฿1,800/night, scored 8.7 out of 10 from 489 reviews on Trip.com.

Outdoor swimming pool at The Davis Bangkok surrounded by tropical trees and sun loungers

body.html: The Davis Bangkok tells a story that's rare on Sukhumvit — East meeting West, with the past walking comfortably beside the present. The estate spans two distinct wings: the contemporary Corner Wing with 247 well-appointed rooms, and Baan Davis, a collection of traditional Thai-style residences with 2 or 3 bedrooms, private gardens and, in select villas, their own pool. The design ethos throughout is measured: classical stone and dark timber on the façade, wide corridors, and room proportions that feel genuinely generous rather than just well-photographed.

Spaciousness is the detail guests mention most in reviews. The Deluxe rooms in Corner Wing start at 45–55 sqm — noticeably larger than the Bangkok four-star average — while the Two-Bedroom Suites run to 130–145 sqm. When you factor in the price-per-square-metre, multiple reviewers note that The Davis delivers value that larger international-brand competitors in the same price bracket rarely match.
"Huge rooms, spotlessly clean, and the garden atmosphere makes you forget you're in the middle of Sukhumvit. Staff spoke excellent English and were genuinely attentive."

The Phrom Phong location comes with real advantages. Emporium Mall is 13 minutes on foot, EmQuartier a short stroll or five-minute Grab beyond that, and EmSphere completes the EM District trifecta further along. Sukhumvit Soi 24 is organically Bangkok's most concentrated Japanese quarter — authentic ramen, izakaya, yakitori and matcha cafes line both sides of the soi, making the hotel a natural base for anyone who loves Japanese food without flying to Tokyo. Benjasiri Park, a calm greenspace popular with morning joggers, sits barely eight minutes away on foot.

Two facts worth knowing before you book. First, BTS Phrom Phong station is 1.3 km away — roughly 13–15 minutes walking in Bangkok's heat, which adds up quickly if you plan to ride the skytrain every day. The hotel runs shuttle transfers and Grab is cheap, but it's a genuine consideration compared to hotels in Soi 22 or 26 that sit closer to the station. Second, 24 BLVD, the hotel's entertainment zone between the two buildings, houses Baccarat nightclub. Reviews consistently flag that rooms facing this area can hear thumping music until 3–4 a.m. on busy nights. A direct conversation with reservations about your room assignment goes a long way.

Facilities are extensive for the price point: two outdoor pools (including a rooftop pool with city views), spa, sauna, four Jacuzzis, a well-equipped gym, and the Fairway Golf & City Club for those who want to keep their swing sharp mid-trip. On the dining side, Gallery Cafe offers Asian and international buffet spreads, AMORE handles comfort food, HONE IZAKAYA covers Japanese yakitori, and an on-site Starbucks handles the breakfast rush. Breakfast reviews are mixed — adequate spread covering Thai, Asian and Western options, but nothing guests single out as exceptional.

Being honest about the trade-offs: parts of the property show their age. Some rooms and common areas have been partially renovated while others carry the look of an older build that hasn't been fully refreshed. A subset of reviews mentions maintenance issues — a broken window latch, a noisy air-conditioning unit, curtains that don't fully block light. None of these are catastrophic, and the overall score of 8.7 suggests most guests leave satisfied, but they're worth factoring in if you're a light sleeper or someone who prefers brand-new interiors.

Rates for Deluxe rooms in Corner Wing typically run ฿1,800–3,500/night depending on season, with the low season often dipping below that range. Baan Davis Two-Bedroom Suites sit around ฿4,500–7,000. Thai Three-Bedroom Villas start at approximately ฿6,500. Prices vary considerably across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com — always compare before committing, as the spread between platforms can be significant.

highlights.title: 2.3-Acre Garden Estate in Sukhumvit
highlights.text: Two pools, a full spa, Baan Davis Thai villas and lush greenery — an atmosphere almost no other hotel in mid-Sukhumvit can replicate at this price.

highlights.title: Rooms Larger Than the Bangkok Average
highlights.text: Deluxe rooms at 45–55 sqm are meaningfully bigger than competitors at the same price point. Reviewers consistently call out the value for space.

highlights.title: 13-Minute Walk to Emporium
highlights.text: Emporium, EmQuartier, EmSphere — the full EM District is walking distance. So is Sukhumvit Soi 24's Japanese quarter, one of Bangkok's best for authentic ramen and izakaya.

honestSummary: The Davis Bangkok delivers generous room sizes, rare garden greenery, two pools and a full spa at a mid-range four-star price in the heart of the EM District. The trade-offs are real: BTS isn't walking distance, parts of the property show age, and rooms near the nightclub can be noisy at night. Know those in advance and it's a strong option for travellers who want space and atmosphere over a lobby-level brand name.
honestChecks: If you need to step off a BTS in 2 minutes each morning — The Davis isn't the most convenient choice for that. Consider hotels on Soi 22 or Soi 26 that sit closer to Phrom Phong station.
If you're a light sleeper — specify at booking that you want a quiet room away from 24 BLVD. The hotel can accommodate this but you need to ask.
If you're travelling as a family or group wanting your own space — Baan Davis Thai villas are excellent but book early; there are limited units and they sell out.

tips.title: Request a Quiet Room Away from 24 BLVD
tips.body: Ask at booking — or at check-in — for a room not facing the entertainment zone between the two buildings. The hotel can usually accommodate this, and it makes a real difference to sleep quality.

tips.title: Use Grab Rather Than Walking to BTS
tips.body: The 1.3 km to BTS Phrom Phong is manageable in cool weather but uncomfortable in Bangkok's heat. Grab is cheap (฿40–60) and the hotel also offers transfer services worth asking about.

tips.title: Explore Sukhumvit Soi 24's Japanese Quarter
tips.body: Soi 24 is Bangkok's most concentrated Japanese dining strip — authentic ramen, izakaya and yakitori right outside the hotel gates. Budget an evening just for walking the soi.

tips.title: Use the Rooftop Pool in the Morning
tips.body: The rooftop pool has the best city views, and early morning — before the Bangkok heat kicks in — is the most pleasant time. The garden-level pool stays shaded and is better for a long afternoon float.

faq.q: Where is The Davis Bangkok and how far is it from BTS Phrom Phong?
faq.a: The Davis Bangkok is at 88 Sukhumvit Soi 24, Khlong Toei, Bangkok 10110. BTS Phrom Phong station is 1.3 km away — about 13–15 minutes walking, or a 5-minute Grab ride. Emporium Shopping Mall is a 13-minute walk.

faq.q: Does The Davis Bangkok have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has two outdoor swimming pools: a garden-level pool surrounded by tropical greenery and a rooftop pool with city views. Additional facilities include 4 Jacuzzis, a sauna and a full-service spa.

faq.q: What is Baan Davis and who is it for?
faq.a: Baan Davis is the hotel's traditional Thai villa section — standalone 2–3 bedroom residences with private gardens, full kitchens and, in some villas, a private pool. They're well-suited to families, groups or anyone wanting a home-like experience rather than a standard hotel room. Rates start from around ฿6,500/night.

faq.q: Is noise from the nightclub a problem at The Davis Bangkok?
faq.a: It can be. 24 BLVD and Baccarat nightclub, located between the hotel's two buildings, operate late into the night on busy evenings. Some guest rooms facing that zone report hearing music until 3–4 a.m. The best approach: tell reservations you want a quiet room away from the entertainment area before you arrive.

faq.q: What are the typical room rates at The Davis Bangkok?
faq.a: Deluxe rooms in Corner Wing typically start around ฿1,800–2,200/night in low season and can reach ฿3,500 in peak periods. Baan Davis Two-Bedroom Suites run ฿4,500–7,000. Always compare Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com — prices vary significantly across platforms.

quickAnswerH2: What is The Davis Bangkok and who is it best for?
quickAnswerHtml: The Davis Bangkok is a 4-star boutique hotel on a 2.3-acre estate at Sukhumvit Soi 24, Phrom Phong. It offers 247 rooms and traditional Thai-style Baan Davis villas, two outdoor pools, a spa and fitness facilities. It's best for travellers who want generous space and a resort-like atmosphere in a prime EM District location, from approx. ฿1,800/night.
